author: Ayush Sharma
title: Ronald Araújo Returns to Uruguay Training After Fitness Scare
deck: A difficult finish to Uruguay’s win over Argentina raised questions about Ronald Araújo’s condition, but the Liverpool defender’s return to training offered an encouraging early sign.
label: Liverpool injury news
seoTitle: Ronald Araújo Injury Update: Liverpool Defender Trains With Uruguay
metaDescription: Ronald Araújo trained with Uruguay after reportedly struggling to walk following the Argentina friendly. We explain the concern and Liverpool implications.

body.text: Ronald Araújo has given Liverpool an encouraging sign after a fitness scare during Uruguay’s international window. The defender was reported to have finished the 2-1 win over Argentina walking with difficulty after a challenge involving Julián Álvarez. That description naturally created concern at Anfield, particularly because Araújo has become an important part of Andoni Iraola’s defensive structure. A subsequent training image offered reassurance, although it was not the same as formal confirmation that he was fully fit for club duty.
A strong performance against Argentina, then a worrying report

Araújo started at centre-back in Uruguay’s meeting with Argentina at La Bombonera. He played an important part in the opening goal, winning the initial aerial contest that led to Leonardo Balerdi’s own goal. Uruguay went on to win 2-1, giving the defender and his teammates a result to celebrate in one of South America’s most demanding away environments.

The concern came after the final whistle. Uruguayan outlet El Observador reported that Araújo had finished the match walking with difficulty after a challenge on Álvarez. That description raised the possibility of a knock, but it did not establish a specific diagnosis or confirm a serious injury. There was no reason to treat the report as proof of a long absence.
The training picture changes the mood

Araújo later shared an image of himself back in Uruguay training. That was an encouraging development because it suggested he had not been forced into immediate withdrawal from the national-team camp. It was still only an early indicator. A player can complete part of a training session while managing discomfort, and the true picture depends on how he responds to the next workload and whether the medical staff consider him ready for match action.

Uruguay were scheduled to face the Dominican Republic in another friendly on 18 November. That match gave the national-team staff a final opportunity to assess the defender before he returned to Liverpool. The club would want him to travel back promptly and provide a clear report on his condition, especially with the Premier League programme resuming shortly afterwards.
Why Liverpool value his physical profile

Araújo has brought size, aggression and aerial presence to Liverpool’s back line. At around 6ft 3in, he gives the team another strong defender when opponents deliver crosses or target the far post. The reported 4.2 aerial duels won per 90 minutes in league play places him among the strongest defenders in that category, according to the data cited in the original report. His value is not limited to heading the ball: his presence can change where the opposition chooses to attack.
His role has become difficult to replace

Liverpool’s defensive structure has been affected by absences and the need to balance centre-back and full-back positions. Araújo’s ability to cover at right-back gives Iraola another option when the team wants to strengthen the defensive side of that flank. He can defend wide spaces, compete physically and still help the team build from the back. That versatility is particularly useful when opponents try to overload one side or target the space behind an adventurous full-back.

The danger of relying too heavily on one player is obvious. If Araújo is unavailable, Liverpool may have to change the profile of the right-back, alter the way the centre-backs defend crosses or ask a midfielder to cover a wider zone. Those adjustments can work, but they change the team’s balance. That is why the club will want a clear understanding of his fitness rather than simply hoping the training image tells the whole story.
What the next update should clarify

The key questions are straightforward: did Araújo complete the full training session, did he experience any reaction after the Argentina match and is he available for Uruguay’s next fixture? Liverpool will then need to assess travel, recovery and match readiness before deciding on his involvement against Manchester United. The international staff cannot make that club decision on their own.
Encouraging, but not yet a medical all-clear

The return to training is positive and should reduce immediate alarm, but it is too early to declare the episode completely resolved. No specific injury diagnosis has been confirmed in the reporting, and a training photograph is not a medical bulletin. The responsible conclusion is that Liverpool have received an encouraging sign while awaiting a fuller assessment.

Araújo’s importance to the side makes the update worth following, but it should not be exaggerated into a crisis. Liverpool need him healthy over the whole season, not simply available for one weekend. The next reliable information should come from the player’s condition after the Uruguay camp and the club’s own medical checks.

author: Ayush Sharma
title: Takumi Minamino’s Most Unusual Record: 187 High-Fives in One Minute
deck: Before his Liverpool goals and Premier League medal, Takumi Minamino had already achieved a world record in Japan — one that required speed, stamina and hundreds of smiling strangers.
label: Football stories
seoTitle: Takumi Minamino Guinness World Record: 187 High-Fives in a Minute
metaDescription: The story of Takumi Minamino’s Guinness World Record for 187 high-fives in one minute, his Liverpool career and his return from injury at Monaco.

facts.label: Year of the Cerezo Osaka community event

body.text: Footballers collect medals, caps and goals, but Takumi Minamino has a record that is unlikely to appear in a normal career profile. Before he became a Liverpool player, the Japan international achieved a Guinness World Record by delivering 187 high-fives in one minute. It is a wonderfully unusual piece of football trivia, but the story says something about the community role players can have and the unexpected moments that stay with them long after a transfer or a trophy.
A community event in Osaka produced a world record

The record attempt took place in 2014, when Minamino was an 18-year-old at Cerezo Osaka, his first professional club. The club organised a community event at a local shopping centre, where hundreds of residents queued to meet the players. Minamino was asked to move down the line and high-five as many people as possible in one minute. He managed 187, enough to earn the unusual record.

Minamino later recalled the event in an interview with Liverpool’s official website. Around 200 people had queued, and he was selected partly because he was the youngest player in the team. He described it as a very good memory, adding that it remained a subject of conversation among the players. It was not a sporting record based on speed over distance or strength in a gym. It was a small community challenge that became part of the player’s personal history.
Why 187 high-fives became a Guinness achievement

The task sounds simple until it is placed under a strict one-minute limit. Minamino had to move quickly, make contact with each participant and avoid losing time between people. The event required coordination rather than elite football technique, but it still depended on timing and concentration. A record attempt also needs a clear method of counting so that the final number can be verified.

The record was later surpassed by Kaiser Permanente, whose team achieved 290 high-fives in one minute in 2016. Minamino’s achievement therefore belongs to an earlier chapter of the record’s history. It remains a fun footnote rather than a current world-record claim, and that distinction matters when the story is retold.
A record that fits his reputation

Minamino has often been described as energetic, willing to work and comfortable moving between different roles. Those qualities were visible in his playing style, but the high-five story offers a lighter illustration of the same willingness to take part. It is also an example of a football club using its players to build a connection with local supporters away from the pitch.
From Cerezo Osaka to Anfield

Minamino’s career took him from Japan to Europe, first with Red Bull Salzburg and then Liverpool. He joined the Reds in January 2020, arriving in the middle of a season that would end with the club winning the Premier League. He made 55 appearances and scored 14 goals across competitions before moving to Monaco in 2022. His Liverpool role was not always straightforward, but he contributed in cup competitions and provided useful depth during a period of intense fixture congestion.

His time at Anfield included a league winner’s medal, but he was not simply a trophy collector. Minamino worked across the front line, pressed aggressively and offered a different type of movement to the established attackers. He was often used from the bench, yet he found ways to influence games in domestic cups and in moments when Liverpool needed energy and intelligent runs.
The Monaco chapter and the challenge of returning

At Monaco, Minamino developed a more regular role and became a familiar attacking presence in Ligue 1. A serious knee injury disrupted that progress and kept him out for a long period. His return in October 2026, when he played 59 minutes in a European Conference League victory over CSKA Sofia, marked the end of an absence reported at 298 days. That was a significant personal milestone after months of rehabilitation.

The injury also affected his international prospects and interrupted the rhythm that he had built at club level. A player returning from an ACL problem must regain more than fitness. He has to rebuild confidence in sharp changes of direction, trust the operated knee in contact and adapt to the speed of competitive football. Each appearance is part of that process, and the minutes need to be managed carefully.
A small story from a career still being written

The high-five record is not a measure of Minamino’s footballing quality, but it is a human detail that makes his career more memorable. It connects the teenager at a shopping centre in Osaka to the forward who later celebrated major honours at Liverpool and fought his way back from injury at Monaco.

Football is full of stories that never appear on a tactics board or in a transfer fee. Minamino’s 187 high-fives are one of them: a quick, joyful community moment that travelled with him across continents. The record has been broken, the career has moved on and the player has returned from a difficult setback. Yet the story still offers a reminder that footballers are part of communities as well as teams — and that sometimes the most memorable achievement is the one nobody expects.
